title: Realtime chat benchmark orchestration for SSE & WebSocket at scale
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an extensible load-testing orchestration layer and artifact suite for realtime chat/completions (SSE and WebSocket) that can emulate production traffic shapes, measure throughput and tail latency (tokens/sec, p95/p99), and detect regressions automatically. The harness must support: multi-protocol drivers (SSE + WSS), realistic user typing models, KV-cache warm-up and cold-start scenarios, per-connection multiplexing, and configurable failure injection (partial connection drops, HTTP 5xx). Output artifacts should include time-series metrics, per-run histograms, and a regression alerting dashboard integrated with our monitoring stack.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Baseline workload generator supporting SSE and WebSocket with configurable concurrency and token emission rates
A2: Measurement pipeline emits tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, server-side 5xx rate, and tail token burst stats to our metrics cluster
A3: Regression detection: historical baseline ingestion + automated statistical test (alpha=0.01) that raises an alert when p95 latency or tokens/sec regresses beyond configured thresholds
A4: Orchestrator can run multi-region scenarios and produce per-region breakdowns in CSV/JSON
A5: Reproducible run artifact (config, seed, commit) stored in S3 with linkable dashboard and a PR template to attach results
steps: Design driver API for protocol-agnostic workload specification (input template, token distribution, typing model). See design doc link.
Implement SSE driver and separate WebSocket driver with a shared core for message pacing and KV state handling.
Add features to emulate: short chat turns (<=64 tokens), long-form completions (>=512 tokens), and streaming interruptions (client disconnect mid-stream).
Hook metrics emitter: emit per-connection and aggregated metrics to metrics cluster (prometheus pushgateway -> our observability stack).
Implement regression detector: bootstrap baseline from last 30 runs, compute non-parametric confidence intervals, and push alerts to #benchmarks and PagerDuty if drift detected.
Run parallel smoke tests and then full scale runs on dedicated capacity with increasing concurrency in 3 stages (10%, 50%, 100% target load).
Publish run artifacts and update benchmark dashboard with annotated regressions and linked PRs.
metrics: generation_latency_ms: p50, p90, p95, p99 (end-to-end from request start to final token sent)
streaming_token_latency_ms (time between server emitting successive tokens)
variance and skew of tokens_per_request distribution
design_notes: We chose a modular driver pattern to keep protocol-specific logic thin; core pacing, sampling, and result aggregation live in a single component to ensure consistent metrics across SSE and WSS.
Typing model: use a two-component Poisson process to simulate typing bursts and pauses; parameterizable per-workload to match product telemetry (e.g., mobile vs desktop patterns).

Regression detection: prefer non-parametric (bootstrap) and EWMA combined approach — bootstrap for initial baseline CI, EWMA for online drift detection. This reduces sensitivity to non-normal latency distributions common in GPU-backed inference.
Stateful scenarios: include KV-cache warmup steps where we pre-prime caches for a configurable subset of requests to measure warm vs cold delta.
risks: Running large-scale WSS/SSE tests can exhaust shared network bandwidth in dedicated clusters — coordinate with infra before 100% runs.
False positives in regression detection if baseline window contains noisy outliers; mitigate via outlier trimming and minimum-run thresholds.
Driver resource usage (CPU/FDs) may bias client-side metrics if not isolated; we will run drivers on separate host pools.
